paragraphs: Rabbi Elazar Hammodai, Avot, chapter 3. Rashi, Bava Batra 10, end of b: he was from Mount Modai. He prayed that Hadrian not capture Betar, and Hadrian could not. A Kuti slandered him to ben Koziva, saying he wanted peace with Hadrian; ben Koziva killed him. A heavenly voice then cried, “Woe, worthless shepherd! A sword against his arm and right eye,” for Elazar Hammodai was Israel’s arm and right eye. Betar fell that day, Eikhah Midrash, “The Lord swallowed up,” fifty-two or seventy-three years after the Temple’s destruction. He was Yochanan ben Zakkai’s student. Yuchasin, Rema’s Yesod Olam glosses, calls him his colleague—requires examination. S.Ma.’s introduction [סמ״ע; work siglum unresolved] lists the second postdestruction generation: Tarfon, Akiva, Elazar Hammodai, Ammihud (see there). His colleague Yishmael; Tarfon too, though he calls Tarfon “my teacher,” while Tarfon calls him “Modai,” Yoma 76a. Elazar ben Perata in his name; In Shevuat Ha'edut, Elazar ben Azaryah and Chananya, Rabbi Yehoshua’s nephew, report in his name [the Bavli reads Chanina, and the printed Heilprin has an extra ben before Chananya]. He was an expositor: “We still need the Modai,” Shabbat 55b. His grave in Kefar Gevartayin is with Yaakov of Gevurya, one monument over both, Gelilot Eretz Yisrael [גא״י; reading provisional].
